name: TextButton
simple: A TextButton is a box with text that players can click or tap. It looks like a TextLabel but also has button events like Activated. Use it for Play, Buy, Close, and any other clickable word.
analogy: A TextButton is like an elevator button with a label on it: it shows words like 'Lobby' and does something when you press it.
where: Inside a ScreenGui (or a SurfaceGui/BillboardGui that's in PlayerGui). The click code must be in a LocalScript, often placed right inside the button in StarterGui.

terms.UI / GUI: User Interface: the buttons, menus, text and pictures drawn on the screen or on things in the game.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. All UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.ScreenGui: The invisible container that holds UI shown on the player's screen. It must be inside the player's PlayerGui (put it in StarterGui in Studio).
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside.
terms.UDim2: The value used for Size and Position: (X Scale, X Offset, Y Scale, Y Offset). Scale is a fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size; Offset is exact pixels.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible.
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green and blue amounts, like Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) for red.
terms.font: The style of the letters, like Arial, Comic, or a blocky game font.
terms.rich text: Text with simple tags inside it, like word, that make parts bold, italic or colored.
terms.grapheme: One visible character, like a letter, a number, or a symbol.
terms.wrap: When text reaches the edge, it continues on the next line.
terms.truncate: Cut off text that's too long, often adding '...' at the end.
terms.read-only: You can read the value but not change it.
terms.localization: Translating text into the player's language.
terms.deprecated: Old and replaced by something better. Don't use it in new code.
terms.Activated: The button's main 'pressed' event. Works with mouse, touch and gamepad.
terms.RemoteEvent: A messenger that lets a LocalScript tell the server something happened, like 'I clicked Buy'.
terms.server: Roblox's computer that runs the game for everyone. Important things like giving coins must happen there.

examples.title: A button that opens and closes a menu
examples.place: LocalScript inside a TextButton, in a ScreenGui in StarterGui that also has a Frame named "Menu"
examples.code:
local button = script.Parent
local menu = button.Parent:WaitForChild("Menu")

menu.Visible = false
button.Text = "Open Menu"

button.Activated:Connect(function()
	menu.Visible = not menu.Visible -- flip between shown and hidden
	if menu.Visible then
		button.Text = "Close Menu"
	else
		button.Text = "Open Menu"
	end
end)
explain: button.Parent is the ScreenGui, where we find the Menu frame.
Activated fires on click, tap, or gamepad A press.
'not menu.Visible' flips true to false and false to true, so each press toggles the menu.
We also change the button's text so players know what it will do next.

gotchas: Click code must run in a LocalScript. To change coins or give items, send a RemoteEvent to the server.
Use Activated, not MouseButton1Click, so phone and console players can press it too.
Want a plain rectangle button without words? Set TextTransparency to 1 or leave Text empty.

TextButton.ContentText.simple: Read-only. The text exactly as players see it. If RichText is on, the formatting tags like are removed. For Text = "Hi" with RichText on, ContentText is "Hi".

TextButton.Font.simple: Picks a built-in font from a list (Enum.Font), like Gotham or Cartoon. It stays in sync with FontFace; FontFace is the newer, more flexible choice.

TextButton.FontFace.simple: The font used to draw the text, including its weight (how bold) and style (italic). It can use fonts that aren't in the old Font list.
TextButton.FontFace.example:
local button = script.Parent
button.FontFace = Font.new("rbxasset://fonts/families/FredokaOne.json")
-- A bold font: pass the weight when you make it
button.FontFace = Font.new("rbxasset://fonts/families/GothamSSm.json", Enum.FontWeight.Bold)

TextButton.LineHeight.simple: The space between lines of text, as a multiplier from 1 to 3. 1 is normal, 1.5 adds extra breathing room, 2 is double spacing.

TextButton.LocalizedText.simple: Read-only. The translated text actually being shown, when automatic translation (AutoLocalize) found a translation for the player's language. If no translation applies, it's just the normal text.

TextButton.MaxVisibleGraphemes.simple: Limits how many characters are shown. -1 (default) shows everything. Count up from 0 to make a 'typewriter' effect where letters appear one by one.
TextButton.MaxVisibleGraphemes.example:
local button = script.Parent
button.Text = "Welcome, adventurer!"
for i = 0, #button.Text do
	button.MaxVisibleGraphemes = i
	task.wait(0.05)
end
button.MaxVisibleGraphemes = -1 -- show everything
TextButton.MaxVisibleGraphemes.gotcha: The text layout doesn't move while letters appear; it's planned as if all the text is already there.

TextButton.OpenTypeFeatures.simple: Turns on special font features using short codes separated by commas, like "zero" for a zero with a slash through it. Empty (default) means none. If a code doesn't work, OpenTypeFeaturesError says why.
TextButton.OpenTypeFeatures.example:
local button = script.Parent
button.OpenTypeFeatures = "zero" -- slashed zeros, so 0 doesn't look like O

TextButton.OpenTypeFeaturesError.simple: Read-only. Empty when OpenTypeFeatures worked. Otherwise a message like "Unsupported feature: xyz" telling you what went wrong.
TextButton.OpenTypeFeaturesError.example:
local button = script.Parent
if button.OpenTypeFeaturesError ~= "" then
	warn(button.OpenTypeFeaturesError)
end

TextButton.RichText.simple: When true, you can style parts of the text with tags like bold, italic or red.
TextButton.RichText.example: local button = script.Parent button.RichText = true button.Text = "You found a golden sword!"

TextButton.Text.simple: The words shown. You can use \n in a script to start a new line.
TextButton.Text.example:
local button = script.Parent
button.Text = "Line one\nLine two"

TextButton.TextBounds.simple: Read-only. The size in pixels of the box the text actually needs. Handy for making a background exactly fit the text.
TextButton.TextBounds.example:
local button = script.Parent
print("Text needs", button.TextBounds.X, "by", button.TextBounds.Y, "pixels")

TextButton.TextColor3.example:
local button = script.Parent
button.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255) -- white text

TextButton.TextDirection.simple: Which way the text reads. Auto (default) figures it out from the language, so languages like Arabic read right-to-left. You can force LeftToRight or RightToLeft.

TextButton.TextFits.simple: Read-only. true if all the text fits inside, false if some of it is cut off.
TextButton.TextFits.example:
local button = script.Parent
if not button.TextFits then
	print("Text is too long for this box!")
end

TextButton.TextScaled.simple: When true, the text automatically grows or shrinks to fill the whole box (TextSize is ignored and wrapping turns on). Great for BillboardGuis and SurfaceGuis.
TextButton.TextScaled.gotcha: Text can become tiny and hard to read. Add a UITextSizeConstraint to set a min/max size, and don't combine it with AutomaticSize.

TextButton.TextSize.simple: How tall one line of text is, in pixels. 14 is small, 24 is medium, 48 is big. Ignored when TextScaled is on.
TextButton.TextSize.gotcha: Try not to go below 9; tiny text is hard to read for many players.

TextButton.TextStrokeColor3.simple: The color of the outline drawn around each letter. Only shows when TextStrokeTransparency is less than 1.
TextButton.TextStrokeColor3.example:
local button = script.Parent
button.TextStrokeColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0) -- black outline
button.TextStrokeTransparency = 0             -- make it visible
TextButton.TextStrokeColor3.gotcha: For thicker or gradient outlines, use a UIStroke instead.

TextButton.TextStrokeTransparency.simple: How see-through the letter outline is. 1 (default) = no outline, 0 = solid outline. The outline is drawn several times stacked, so even 0.5 looks quite solid; 0.75 to 1 gives a soft outline.

TextButton.TextTransparency.simple: How see-through the text is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible. Doesn't affect the background box (that's BackgroundTransparency).
TextButton.TextTransparency.example:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local button = script.Parent
-- Fade the text out over 1 second
TweenService:Create(button, TweenInfo.new(1), {TextTransparency = 1}):Play()

TextButton.TextTruncate.simple: What to do with text that's too long to fit. None (default) just cuts it off. AtEnd replaces the end with "...". SplitWord can cut in the middle of a word.
TextButton.TextTruncate.example:
local button = script.Parent
button.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd -- "A really long na..."

TextButton.TextWrapped.simple: When true, long text continues on the next line instead of running off the side. It prefers to break at spaces. Lines that don't fit vertically aren't shown.

TextButton.TextXAlignment.simple: Lines the text up sideways inside the box: Left, Center (default) or Right.

TextButton.TextYAlignment.simple: Lines the text up up-and-down inside the box: Top, Center (default) or Bottom.
